A share-ride transportation service required by the ADA for individuals who
cannot use fixed-route services because of a disability.

Communicated time at which the ADA paratransit rider has a scheduled
obligation at his or her destination, such as, but not limited to, medical
appointment or the start of work.

A paratransit trip where multiple passengers are transported on the same
vehicle

Service data across the entire paratransit system, including On-time pickup
rates; denials, Missed Trips, No-shows, Complaints, etc.

When the agency cannot schedule a requested trip to include refusal,
offering unacceptable times; excessive delays that effectively prevent
travel. Examples of trip denials include: A rider requests a next-day trip, and
the transit agency says it cannot provide that trip. Or A rider requests a next-
day trip, and the transit agency can only offer a trip that is outside of the 1-
hour negotiating window. Or A rider requests a round-trip and the agency
can only provide on leg of the trip. If the rider does not take the offered on-
way trip, both portions of the trip are denial.
